Account summary: RivetLoop is a mid-market product analytics SaaS building an in-app onboarding copilot to drive user activation. Primary ask: low-variance streaming chat + tool-calling for guided flows (open URL, fetch user profile, create milestone). Initial preference: evaluate Redwood Hosted API for speed to market, run 2-week POC, then move to Dedicated if SLOs + pricing acceptable.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-17: Intro demo (Aisha + Marco) — showed Redwood hosted streaming and function calls. Positive reaction to streaming latency demo.
- 2026-02-18: Discovery call (Fireflies ff_20260218_921) — product team provided expected qps and sample flows. Latency target: first-byte streaming <= 180-250ms for interactive flows; end-to-end session median <1s for short prompts.
- 2026-02-22: Sent POC design doc + sample prompts (drive link). Requested token cap controls for onboarding flows.

Technical / requirements notes:
- Workload: high-concurrency interactive onboarding sequences; typical session length 80-400 tokens, most flows <200 tokens.
- QPS: expected bursty daytime traffic, avg concurrent sessions ~60-120 during peaks (one region).
- Latency SLO: target first-token streaming <=200ms median, 95th <=350ms. Consistent tail latency is mandatory — product UX suffers with jitter.
- Tool calling: need reliable function/tool call round trips; want deterministic fallbacks when external tool times out.
- Cost control: strict token caps per flow & per-user monthly budget. Need billing visibility at route/token level.
- Model preference: open to Llama-family quantized variants; will test Redwood verified models and possibly a larger model for complex flows.
- Caching: interested in prefix/KV caching to reduce cost for repeat flows. Want Redwood to show expected cost drop with caching in POC.

Commercial / buying signals:
- Interested in Hosted API for POC; strong intent to evaluate Dedicated within 6-10 weeks if SLOs met. Budget for 12-month commit likely in $50k-$150k ARR band.
- Procurement will require legal review (standard enterprise terms) and clear SLA language for latency.

- "Show us predictable tail latency and per-route cost controls; otherwise we can't commit to a reserve." — CTO.
